_comment: Service-test-harness allowlist profile. See docs/SERVICE_TESTING.md. Copy the allowed_commands entries into your own agent_config.json; the connection fields here are placeholders. Every args_regex is anchored to the WHOLE joined argument string by the agent, so these patterns match exactly what they read.

allowed_commands._comment: FAULT INJECTION. One script, fixed verb set, self-reverting. Durations are capped at 300s inside the script AND by this regex (1-3 digits).
allowed_commands.name: /opt/myrmex/chaos.sh

allowed_commands._comment: PROBE the service under test, and any OTHER service reachable from this host. This is the 'use the host as a vantage point' capability - no proxy needed. Pin the hosts you actually test against; a bare .+ here turns the agent into a request forwarder. NOTE: ONE entry per command name - the allowlist matches the FIRST entry whose name matches and stops, so a second `curl` entry would be dead config. Add probe variants as alternations here, not as new entries.
allowed_commands.name: curl

allowed_commands._comment: TCP reachability to a dependency (is the DB even listening?).
allowed_commands.name: nc

allowed_commands._comment: DNS resolution check - the failure nobody suspects until they do.
allowed_commands.name: dig

allowed_commands._comment: APPLY a config change between test iterations. The script owns WHAT may change; this regex only picks which named variant. This is how you 'make changes while testing' without a file_write tool.
allowed_commands.name: /opt/myrmex/apply-config.sh

allowed_commands._comment: Service lifecycle. service_control covers start/stop/restart/status for these too; this entry is for the non-systemd case.
allowed_commands.name: systemctl

allowed_commands._comment: READ-ONLY diagnostics. Safe to grant broadly.
allowed_commands.name: journalctl
